title: David Fincher Brushes off AI Backlash Over Brad Pitt’s New Cliff Booth Movie
summary: David Fincher refuses to apologize for using AI in his latest Brad Pitt film. The director says critics have turned a technical choice into a culture war, and he insists the technology served the storytelling rather than replacing the people who make movies. David Fincher defends AI’s future in filmmaking Fincher pushed back against the […] The post David Fincher Brushes off AI Backlash Over Brad Pitt’s New Cliff Booth Movie appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More .
content: Photo Credit: Netflix David Fincher refuses to apologize for using AI in his latest Brad Pitt film. The director says critics have turned a technical choice into a culture war, and he insists the technology served the storytelling rather than replacing the people who make movies. David Fincher defends AI’s future in filmmaking Fincher pushed back against the uproar over The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth during an interview with El País 50 . Asked whether he anticipated the heated debate about AI reconstructing a version of Los Angeles and its television footage, he rejected the premise outright. “You know what the thing is? The debate over AI masks a culture war; it has nothing to do with movies,” he said. “I’ve never been in a situation where people cared about the tools I used.” The director framed his priority plainly: tell the story with the budget and schedule available. He noted that every production involves shooting a set number of sequences and animating them, and AI simply joined that toolkit. Fincher first confirmed the AI work on The Ringer ‘s Big Picture podcast, telling host Sean Fennessey that the technology synced a performer’s best vocal take with their best on-camera take when the two didn’t match. He estimated automated dialogue replacement covered just around 5% of the film, with the remainder handled through AI-assisted processes. Actors spent only four or five days re-recording dialogue above scenes. “We could use AI to re-lip that thing,” he said, describing the result as freeing. Fincher also outlined a future in which crews still handcraft sets and shoot masters repeatedly, while AI absorbs technical headaches like focus errors and hair drifting across a lens. “It’ll still be based on real human beings,” he said, adding that actors would repeat actions roughly 15 times instead of far more. Fennessey asked whether that prospect appealed to him. “Totally,” Fincher replied. Not everyone shares his enthusiasm. Early screenings of the Netflix film reportedly set off complaints about visible generative AI. Certain social media users have vowed to skip the Brad Pitt release altogether. Nonetheless, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is currently playing in select IMAX theaters, with a December 23 release set on Netflix. content: Photo Credit: @UniversalPictures / YouTube Christopher Nolan’s 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey brought Homer’s ancient epic to theaters with enormous scale and IMAX photography. Now available on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray and digital platforms, the film raises a question: how should audiences experience it at home? Nolan has an answer. Christopher Nolan recommends using a projector to watch The Odyssey at home Nolan shared his home-viewing philosophy with Polygon, advocating for a setup that mimics the theatrical experience. He pointed to affordable projection technology as a way to elevate living-room screenings. This is the Christopher Nolan-approved way to watch movies at home. @odysseymovie pic.twitter.com/tV0AnS6Ken — Polygon (@Polygon) November 26, 2026 “I’m a big fan of projectors,” Nolan quipped. “You can get a relatively low-cost, pretty high-quality projector dock in your living room, maybe introduce some popcorn into the equation or whatever. You know, have a little mini movie theater.” The director also noted that home viewing enables a different kind of engagement. Audiences can pause, rewind, and study details at their own pace, things a cinema screening doesn’t allow. He added that The Odyssey retains an event-like quality even outside theaters, given its lengthy theatrical run. Universal released the film on November 17 with a 1.78:1 aspect ratio that fills a standard widescreen television. The theatrical IMAX version used a taller 1.43:1 ratio, so the home release trims a small amount of image from the top and bottom. The Odyssey follows Matt Damon’s Odysseus as he fights to return to Ithaca after the Trojan War, battling mythical creatures and dangerous gods along the way. The film’s massive scale and IMAX photography made premium theatrical screenings especially rewarding, and Nolan’s projector suggestion helps narrow the gap between cinema and the living room. Home viewing also lets audiences focus on quieter elements. Damon’s take on Odysseus explores loyalty, identity, and the aftermath of war. Robert Pattinson’s performance and the film’s treatment of Homer’s mythology reward closer attention when spectacle isn’t dominating the screen. The physical release bundles 12 behind-the-scenes featurettes covering the Trojan Horse construction, Moroccan battlefield sets, practical effects, stunts, and Ludwig Göransson’s score. content: Photo Credit: Lionsgate Mckenna Grace treated her role in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping like a mission. The actor, who plays Maysilee Donner and her twin sister Merrilee Donner, came on set with detailed notes and lobbied director Francis Lawrence to preserve small book-accurate touches. She now confirms which details survived the adaptation and why they mattered to her. How Mckenna Grace brought more of Maysilee Donner’s book personality to the screen Grace told PEOPLE that she showed up daily with a list of requests for Lawrence. “Every day I would show up to set with a list of things and thoughts and questions to bother Francis with,” Mckenna Grace quipped. “Yeah, I got the hummingbird, the Mockingjay pins in there. I got my braid.” Her persistence became a running joke among the cast. Whitney Peak, who plays Lenore Dove Baird, recalled Grace carrying a binder and declaring, “‘I need this and this and this and this and this.'” Grace also fought for a subtle costume choice tied to Maysilee’s identity in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping . She wanted different-colored eyeshadows to match each outfit, arguing that Maysilee would cling to her own style no matter what the Capitol imposed. “And so I wanted to find something that differentiated her outfit from just what the Capitol gave her,” Grace explained. Moreover, her push for fidelity grew from long-standing fandom . Grace read all the Hunger Games books while filming one of the Annabelle movies and watched the original films on set. She later questioned Josh Hutcherson about his experience, including whether his days were “as brutally physical as ours, which they were.” Peak credited Grace’s influence, saying Grace was in that writers’ room. Grace agreed that she was really tapped in. Luca Guadagnino is also interested in directing a Bond film Pattinson officially got […] The post Robert Pattinson’s James Bond Has an Oscar-Nominated Director’s Backing appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More .
content: Photo Credit: Warner Bros. Pictures Robert Pattinson will play James Bond , and he already has support from one of cinema’s most respected filmmakers. The casting concludes months of speculation, with Amazon MGM and Denis Villeneuve confirming the star as Daniel Craig’s successor in the legendary 007 franchise. Luca Guadagnino is also interested in directing a Bond film Pattinson officially got the 007 part after a competitive search that reportedly included several British actors. From Jacob Elordi, Jack Lowden, and Callum Turner to Nicholas Hoult and Aaron Taylor-Johnson, the role was in contention before the studio settled on The Odyssey star. Now, Luca Guadagnino has endorsed Pattinson’s selection and shared his own ambitions regarding the franchise. Speaking to Variety at the Marrakech Film Festival, the Italian director called Pattinson “a perfect choice for James Bond.” Guadagnino said, “He’s an incredible star, he’s done so many great roles and I wish someday to work with him, of course.” When asked whether he would direct a Bond film himself, Guadagnino answered affirmatively. “I would say yes, yes, of course,” he stated. “I would like to play with icons.” The director also addressed rumors linking Pattinson to the iconic character Patrick Bateman, clarifying that the actor was never in contention for that part. The director, known for intimate character-driven films, mentioned he hopes his next project will be another love story, though he remains open to the world of James Bond. Robert Pattinson inherits the role after Craig’s five-movie run, which began with Casino Royale and ended with the character’s heroic sacrifice. The new era promises new creative energy, with Pattinson’s star power and Guadagnino’s public backing adding momentum to the franchise’s future. Steven Knight is writing the screenplay. Amy Pascal and David Heyman serve as producers, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. The franchise now operates under Amazon MGM’s creative control following a major deal with longtime producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. content: Photo Credit: Netflix The Hunting Wives Season 2 features another deadly thrill ride through Maple Brook, Texas, and not everyone survives. Episode 6 brings the season’s most shocking moment, and series creator Rebecca Perry Cutter explains why this tragedy had to happen. Rebecca Perry Cutter on the deadly consequences of The Hunting Wives Season 1 Margo comes home from church to find Brad in her living room. She saw him disrupt the service in a hospital gown, begging his father for help, but she missed what happened behind closed doors: Brad shot his father for answering a police call. The two sit down for a calm conversation, yet he soon turns suspicious. Brad starts doubting whether his mother really killed Abby, and when he recalls Margo mentioning an abortion, he accuses her of murder. They both lunge for the gun. Margo wins the race and kills Brad inside her own house. Sophie later backs Margo’s self-defense claim to police. Rebecca Perry Cutter told TVLine she wrote this downfall because George Ferrier “could do more than he did in Season 1,” and he proves it across these six episodes. The creator defends the death as essential storytelling. “I think it’s important that things have consequences,” she says. Brad, she notes, suffered more than anyone in Season 1: his girlfriend died, his mother died, and everyone blamed his mom for murder. Cutter wanted viewers to watch that pain play out rather than disappear. She adds that the character endures trauma, gets sent away by a father who cannot cope, and spirals into ruin. That arc, she says, was something the writers really wanted to explore. Darkness swallows Brad before the end. During an ayahuasca trip, he hallucinates his dead mother Jill, who angrily breastfeeds him and claims he will always belong to her. He bludgeons the vision to death. The Hunting Wives Season 2 episode is now streaming on Netflix.
